note: Per-subpath module graphs. Module count and source bytes ratchet; growth needs a reason.

history.reason: Initial baseline, recorded after M8 S2/S3 landed the directory loader. lokalized/load and lokalized/ssr are still export-{} scaffolds at 1 module each; lokalized/node is 27 modules because the loader composes the shipped parser rather than duplicating it.

M8 S5: lokalized/load's type surface authored from the plan's own TypeScript blocks — CatalogIdentity, StringsManifestV1, FetchEntry, CatalogIdentityInputV1, StringsLoadCoverage, LoadedStrings and LoadFailure. Types only; no runtime, so the graph gains the subpath's own bytes and no new module.

M8 S6: computeCatalogIdentity, plus the synchronous SHA-256 and the bounded RFC 8785 canonicalizer plan 6.1 gives the load graph so identity stays synchronous in a browser. lokalized/load 1 -> 4 modules; the ROOT graph is unchanged at 25 modules, which is the containment claim this ratchet exists to check.

M8 S6b: parseStringsManifest, validateStringsManifest and localeConfigurationForManifest. The load graph gains the bounded JSON path, the CLDR tag data and the locale machinery it validates manifest tags against; the ROOT graph is unchanged.
M8 S7: chain and fetchSet. One module, and the graph barely moves because the candidate sequence is REUSED from src/internal/locale.js rather than reimplemented for the manifest door.

M8 S8: loadStrings and loadEntireManifest. The load graph gains src/parse and its catalog machinery, because a fetched body is parsed by the SAME bounded parser every other door uses rather than a second one.
M8 S9a: the runtime CLDR/data compatibility check plan :1893 requires before catalog I/O. lokalized/load gains src/data/provenance.js — ONE module — which slice S6b had wrongly declared unreachable.
M8 S9: the loaded branch reaches core and therefore every published subpath that re-exports it.

M8 S10: the SSR stamp ships (lokalized/ssr 1 -> 2 modules), and core gains src/internal/runtime-metadata.js — the producer/IANA/corpus identity a stamp must take from the RENDERER, which only works if the renderer holds it. Root/core +1 module; the load subpath grows only by fetch-loader emitting manifestLocaleConfiguration.

M8 S11a: lokalized/node gains the manifest-mediated file loaders, so it now reaches the whole lokalized/load graph (manifest validation, planning, identity, SHA-256, JCS) — 27 -> 37 modules. lokalized/load gains src/load/run-plan.js, the plan runner both doors share: plan order, the concurrency cap, the partial-failure policy, abort and digest-before-parse live in ONE place and the door supplies only a transport.

M8 S11b: the directory walk EXTRACTED to src/node/discovery.js so both Node doors drive one enumeration, plus createStringsManifestFromDirectory. lokalized/node 37 -> 39 modules — discovery.js and manifest-directory.js — and no other subpath moves, because the generator reuses the load graph's identity, SHA-256 and manifest validation rather than duplicating them. (Reason text reconstructed 2026-09-11 after a review session reverted this file by accident; the measured numbers are re-derived from the same source.)
M8 S11b review fixes: normalizedTiebreakers plus the per-file manifest-tag check in the generator, and manifest.js refusing a Map where every read is Object.entries.

M8 S9-owed: core gains the applicable-configuration split (the selection channel reads the full manifest, the resolution channel the loaded catalogs) and the per-use lookup-coverage check. No new module — source only.

M8 close-out: the nine promised-but-undeclared type names land in core and negotiate, and tools/gen-data.js now emits all five fields plan 2.2 declares for DataProvenance (the shipped provenance carried two, so the type could not be declared truthfully).

M8 clause 30: manifest tiebreakers validated against the full manifest (src/load/manifest.js) and filtered to loaded tags in the shared runner (src/load/run-plan.js). No new modules; both graphs grew by the same 5,986 bytes because lokalized/node composes lokalized/load.

M8 clause 22: the plan runner now checks options.signal at the top of its worker loop, so aborting stops ADMISSION rather than relying on the transport to refuse. 748 bytes, no new modules; node composes load.

M8 clause 19: the loaded branch now refuses a record whose two copies of its own warning list disagree (src/internal/loaded-input.js). 3,725 bytes, no new modules; it is in the root graph, so every subpath that composes core moves.

M8 clauses 10 and 33: the Fetch door gained the scheme preflight its Node sibling already had (src/load/fetch-loader.js), and the loaded branch now hands construction the option name it actually reads (src/internal/loaded-input.js).

M8 clause 75: StringsLoadingError gains the construction token StringsParseError has had since M5, and DigestUnavailableError becomes a real Error subclass instead of a plain Error with its name assigned afterwards. No new modules.

S28: src/load/index.js stops DECLARING core's CatalogIdentity and StringsLoadCoverage and consumes them inline, so lokalized/load no longer re-exports the two types plan 3.1 says it must not re-own. The two typedef blocks became prose recording why; +439 B on load, +6 B on node. No module added to any graph.

S29: plan 3.5:1092-1100 declares nine error classes as package exports and the port shipped three. DigestUnavailableError now exports from lokalized/load and ExpressionEvaluationError from lokalized/core; the latter gained the construction token plan 3.5:1107 requires, plus an expressionEvaluationError() factory because it is raised from three modules. No module added to any graph; the growth is the guard, the factory and the prose recording why.

S29: createStrings gains the OPTION UNION plan 3.2:565-588 declares. The port had only the direct arm and read the loaded member through an any cast, so createStrings({ loaded, locale }) -- M8's flagship call -- failed to typecheck for a TypeScript consumer (TS2353). Both arms now spell the other's members never, so a mixed call is refused too. Growth is the two typedefs and the prose recording the defect.
